rows.note:
Confusion family, stated in full: paint-film failure vs wall-surface wear: two degradation items in the same trade (paint_drywall) and tier (work) at severity 1, differing in work_item_code (PAINT_INTERIOR vs DRYWALL_PATCH) and in whether the defect is the coating or the substrate
redfin_10806500 photo_004, kitchen scene, resolution_path llm, routing_reason exact_kind. 2d mapped the observation 'Wall finishes appear tired.' to peeling_or_discolored_paint at rank 7 while wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents sat at rank 6 with kind_ok and scene_ok both true; the 2a prose named the correct reading and only the correct reading ('Visible scuffs, patchy areas, and generally tired finishes suggest prep, repair, and repainting throughout') and the sibling issue on the same photo did resolve to wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, so the better item was reachable and demonstrably selectable in the same run. The reviewer's own lineage note agrees: 'wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents (rank 6) fits the scuffs and patched areas better than a peeling item'. Human truth is misnamed/warranted and the condition was billed (accepted_for_work), so the correction is naming and specificity only: identical kind, severity, tier, scope and package_role, no economics delta. This is the only 2d selection failure in the cluster; the counterexample 4a9736e4 is deliberately NOT filed here because no better item was reachable in its list (all six candidates were degradation items and paint_refresh_recommended was kind-gated with rank null).

Confusion family, stated in full: flooring material: rigid hard flooring vs resilient sheet goods
LEAD-ONLY (evidence_class model_judge, role context): it cannot ground a catalog change and is recorded as a 2d observation only. The reviewer describes a single grey flagstone-printed sheet material torn open in the foreground and along the right perimeter with curled edges and exposed brown backing, with no rigid tiles or planks anywhere - so the resilient item named both material and mechanism better. The better item was fully reachable: rank 2, kind_ok=true, scene_ok=true (reachability_scan). Nothing was lost - Terra supported the selected item and the human agreed (v1_verdict terra_claim_supported, disposition accepted_for_work) - so this is a precision and routing question, not a miss: hard_flooring_broken_or_warped is scope=repair and drives living_repair, while vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted is scope=replace and drives living_modernization. Likely mechanism for the pull, recorded not proven: the hard item's description names vinyl while its atomic_claim does not. Do NOT compensate for this by broadening the catalog. Counter-evidence that 2d is not systematically wrong here: on redfin_11000447 photo_004 2d passed over hard_flooring_broken_or_warped at rank 1 to select vinyl_linoleum_torn_or_lifted at rank 2.

redfin_10952874, photos 025 and 029, both issues (34c681661a9e7f49 and d8fc3b6364d55cc0), resolution_path=llm, routing_reason=exact_kind, candidate_count 7. worn_or_stained_flooring was rank 1 on BOTH issues with kind_ok and scene_ok true, and 2d took rank 3. The photo_029 bullet leads with discoloration and patchy areas - the least scuff-forward wording of the two - and still routed to the scratch/wear item, and 2d itself assigned worn_or_stained_flooring to a sibling bullet on the same photo, so this is a selection failure and not an artifact of 2a's phrasing. The catalog did not invite it: hard_flooring_scratched_or_worn's support_any is scratch / scuff / worn floor / dull finish / worn finish, with no stain or style token, and under the leading-boundary matcher none of those fires on the photo_025 observation, which is consistent with the recorded llm path. Operationally consequential, not equivalent, on mechanism (abrasion versus paint contamination), scope (repair versus replace) and packaging (hard_flooring_scratched_or_worn is bedroom package_driver into bedroom_repair; worn_or_stained_flooring is bedroom package_support into bedroom_modernization). Catalog unchanged.

redfin_80916010 photo_005, issue 14a0ed440898b159. Two defects in one case, both non-catalog. (a) Reachability: older_flooring_style was not in the pool and could not have been - routing_reason=exact_kind on a degradation bullet, all seven candidates degradation, older_flooring_style kind_ok=false (reachability_scan). better_rank is null for that reason, and the best in-pool alternative (worn_or_stained_flooring at rank 2) over-claims wear exactly as the selected item does, so no re-ranking rescues this. (b) Mechanism, now verified rather than assumed: 2d took resolution_path=lexical_shortcut with shortcut_reason=support_phrase_hit, and re-running the shipped matcher (tools/scene_classifier_passes.py::_resolve_candidate_via_lexical_shortcut with tools/pipeline_common.py::term_matches) over the real observation against the item's shipped support_any returns exactly one hit: the bare material token 'vinyl'. Not 'worn vinyl', not 'stained vinyl'; 'worn' is not a token of this item at all, so the case's attribution rationale is wrong about which token fired. The shortcut therefore skipped the LLM entirely and asserted 'staining, discoloration, or wear on intact material' on the strength of a material noun; Terra correctly rejected that claim and a real dated-flooring replacement went unbilled. The actionable owner is the shortcut rule - support_any is documented as a non-gating ranking hint and 125 of 128 items author bare subject nouns into it - not this item's tokens. Suggested 2d-lane fix, for the deferred Pass 2d work and explicitly NOT proposed as a catalog change: require a condition-bearing term match (or subject-plus-condition co-occurrence) before the shortcut may bypass the LLM.

Observation 'The floor has discoloration and staining around the tub and vanity.' (redfin_125779232 photo_007, kind degradation, scene bathroom) resolved to bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn by lexical_shortcut/support_phrase_hit while three flooring items sat in the same frozen top-8 (worn_or_stained_flooring 2, floor_dirty_or_heavily_soiled 3, vinyl_linoleum_worn_or_stained 4, all kind_ok and scene_ok). The reviewer identifies the yellowed blotched sheet vinyl as the genuinely deteriorated component. The correct item was in fact selected for the sibling floor bullets on the same two photos and billed (oc1_df18cf31cc724d4c), so 2d had the answer and used it elsewhere in the same run. Note for the 2d owner: support_phrase_hit only fires on the already top-ranked candidate, so the fix is selection or ranking, not the support list.

Observation 'The ceiling and wall area near the tub look rough.' (redfin_125779232 photo_007) resolved to bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn by lexical_shortcut/support_phrase_hit with bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn at rank 2 and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents at rank 3, both kind_ok and scene_ok. The word 'tub' appears only as a location in the observation. The wall condition was independently billed on the same property via damaged_drywall_or_cracks and wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents, so again nothing was lost - the cost is one extra condition billed under the wrong subject. Same aggregation event as the entry above: four bullets naming three building elements were bound to one condition.

resolution_path lexical_shortcut / support_phrase_hit fired on dated_or_older_windows' bare support_any tokens 'window' and 'windows', pre-empting LLM selection while dated_window_treatment_valance sat at rank 2 and would have named the brown fabric valance the reviewer sees. Logged as a follow-up only: on THIS photo the shortcut's output was Terra-supported and correct (the wood single-hung really is old), so no harm is demonstrated inside this cluster and I am not proposing a change to that item's support_any. Worth watching because the same bare-token shortcut pattern also drove two of the over-bill cards on the other item.

Confusion family, stated in full: exterior walking-surface wear: bare grey weathered wood decking/stair treads vs aged or coating-failed concrete patio-or-porch slab
Two issues on redfin_10735912 - 3cf3f267e567d48d 'The porch floorboards are heavily weathered' (photo_017) and 0916a53bbbd114f9 'The wood front porch is weathered' (photo_028) - resolved via resolution_path llm, routing_reason exact_kind, to rank-1 patio_or_porch_surface_wear while deck_surface_weathering sat at rank 4 with kind_ok true and scene_ok true and no deny_any trigger. The photos show bare unfinished grey wood with raised grain and no coating, so 'clean, sand, stain, refinish' (DECK_REFINISH) is the exact repair and 'resurface or reseal' (SURFACE_RESURFACE) is the approximate one. The selection is broad-but-true rather than wrong, and it is downstream-neutral (both items are severity 1, tier work, scope cosmetic, trade exterior_siding_trim, package_support in exterior_repair), so this is a low-severity 2d specificity follow-up, not a catalog defect. Do not fix it by widening either item: deck_surface_weathering already owns wood decking, and widening patio_or_porch_surface_wear would strand its concrete-slab controls. The third issue on this case, 55f86b711520696c 'Porch and entry details appear aging' on photo_001, is NOT part of this follow-up - photo_001 shows a rowhouse front with no porch, so it is a Pass 2a problem with no correct 2d answer.

Confusion family, stated in full: porch assembly: ceiling/soffit panels vs porch structure vs roofline eave
Issue 79ada05c9fc9051a, observation 'Waviness and sagging are visible around the porch-roof connection.', resolution path llm, routing_reason exact_kind. 2d took rank 1 - an item whose subject is the panels on the UNDERSIDE of the porch roof, which this street-view photo does not show - over rank 3, whose atomic_claim names 'deck or porch structure' with 'loose, rotted, or missing boards' and which matches the reviewer's 'dark, ragged, out-of-plane boards where the porch roof meets the house roof'. Both were kind_ok true and scene_ok true; nothing gated the better choice. Consequence was not cosmetic: the rank-1 claim was unverifiable from this viewpoint, so Terra returned cannot_assess, accepted went false with reason_code verdict_cannot_assess, and a condition the humans called exact and warranted was routed to inspection instead of billed. roofline_water_damage_suspected at rank 4 was the reviewer's other suggestion; I rank it BELOW the rank-3 item because its ontology_basis is moisture_evidence and its claim requires water staining, which the reviewer does not report - selecting it would have traded an unverifiable object for an unverifiable mechanism. Suggested probe for the 2d lane: the pull to rank 1 looks lexical, since soffit_or_porch_ceiling_failed's embed_text contains both 'sagging' and 'porch ceiling' while the better item's embed steers toward walking surfaces; test whether 2d over-weights an embed keyword match against an object the photo cannot show. NOTE that this follow-up is the whole actionable content of the cluster - do not read it as a catalog defect.

Confusion family, stated in full: finished-wall surface damage versus unfinished wall assembly (paint_drywall): patch compound, scraped paint and rough patches versus exposed OSB/sheathing or studs
redfin_10952874 photo_033, issue a33067a74cd038a2, bullet 'An area near the closet corner is unfinished and patchy.' 2c kind defect, scene bedroom, resolution_path llm, shortcut_reason null. 2d took rank 1 (the OSB item) over rank 3 damaged_drywall_or_cracks, which was kind_ok and scene_ok and whose embed_text names 'rough patches' explicitly; Terra then correctly rejected the OSB claim and the real patch-and-paint condition went unbilled. The word 'unfinished' in the bullet is doing the damage: it matches the OSB item's 'Interior wall not finished' embed_text while describing an unfinished PAINT job, not an unfinished wall assembly. Catalog unchanged for this case. Secondary cost worth recording: damaged_drywall_or_cracks is a package_driver for bedroom_repair, so the mis-selection also removed this observation from bedroom package formation, not just from the line-item list.

Lead-graded. Observation 'Masonry walls show discoloration and patching.' - painted basement masonry with blotchy discoloration and patched brick painted over. The subject is masonry, not drywall, and no candidate names patched masonry; peeling_or_discolored_paint at rank 2 names the discoloration better than the rank-1 scuffs item.

Lead-graded. Observation 'Walls have scraped paint and patch areas.' - paint scraped off to white patch compound. Missing paint, not scuffs or dents; the rank-2 item carries PAINT_INTERIOR, the selected one DRYWALL_PATCH.

Lead-graded. Observation 'The left wall has graffiti.' - a roughly four-foot black spray-painted heart and lettering. No item in the 128-item catalog names graffiti; peeling_or_discolored_paint is the nearest reachable home because prime-and-repaint is the repair. Flagged for the coverage discussion, not as a selection error in the narrow sense.

Lead-graded, same unit as the graffiti issue (one condition, not two). Observation 'The right wall has visible patch and roller marks.' - uneven patches with roller texture and sheen differences; a paint-finish defect rather than marks from use.

Lead-graded and partly upstream: the 2a text 'Walls have scuffs, small marks, and inconsistent paint' itself understates paint chipped and flaked to brown substrate behind the radiator, so the retrieval query was weak before 2d ever chose. Contrast with control rc_f468f4066e3f, a correct wall_scuffs use on the same property.

Observation 'Wall surfaces have heavy staining and deteriorated wallboard or paneling.' - heavy brown water staining and torn, delaminating panels exposing bare wood in a basement utility area. Note that wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents' own deny_any contains 'water stain', which the paraphrase 'heavy staining' evaded. Also one of the four promotion photos.

Lead-graded and the second lower-rank case: 2d took wall_scuffs at rank 3 past bathroom_paint_peeling_or_worn at rank 1 and bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn at rank 2. Worth noting for the ceiling half that water_stain_ceiling (severity 3, MOISTURE_REMEDIATION, require_any ['ceiling']) was never retrieved despite being kind- and scene-open.

'uneven' and 'crack' are both in damaged_drywall_or_cracks' support_any and it was gate-open, yet it never entered the top-8; peeling_or_discolored_paint at rank 2 is nearer than the selected item but is not the right home for a crack. Two causes stacked here: understated 2a text and an unreachable better item. One of the four promotion photos.

Neither the rank-2 peeling item nor the selected scuffs item names unfinished/patched drywall; damaged_drywall_or_cracks (support_any 'patch') was gate-open but not retrieved. Confusion family, stated in full: bathroom dated-finish subject confusion: a material-neutral 'wallcovering/finish is dated' observation resolved to a material-specific item that supplies an object word the observation never contained
Issue fe4392d2f287d083, observation 'Wallcovering is dated.', scene bathroom, kind modernization, resolution_path llm, routing_reason exact_kind. Frozen top-8: dated_electrical_outlets_switches 1, dated_wood_paneling 2, vanity_countertop_dated 3, dated_window_treatment_valance 4, dated_wallpaper_present 5, outdated_bathroom_finishes 6, older_flooring_style 7, dated_bathroom_flooring_style 8. 2d took rank 5 over rank 6 although reachability_scan shows outdated_bathroom_finishes with kind_ok true and scene_ok true. The selection rule to examine: when the observation names no material (wallcovering, finish, surface), 2d should prefer the subject-general item (outdated_bathroom_finishes, subject 'bathroom finishes') over any item whose atomic_claim subject asserts a specific material (wallpaper, paneling, tile), because Terra will be asked to verify that material word and the observation gives no basis for it. Note for whoever works this: the most exact item for the true object, vintage_tile_pattern_style (subject 'bathroom tile'), was NOT in the candidate list at all - its require_any ['tile','tiles','tiled'] hard-gated it against a tile-free observation - so 2d could not have chosen it and this follow-up asks only for the rank-6 item it could have chosen. Single occurrence, one property, one photo; treat as a hypothesis to test against other neutral-observation cases, not as a measured rate.

Observation 'White-painted trim appears unfinished in spots.' on a solid limestone rowhouse with no siding anywhere. Frozen list: soffit_or_porch_ceiling_weathered#1, exterior_door_paint_failure#2, baseboard_wear_scuffs#3, shed_exterior_paint_failure#4, exterior_siding_discoloration_fading#5, fence_weathered#6, brick_weathered_or_discolored#7. resolution_path llm, routing_reason exact_kind; the scan records the rank-2 item as kind_ok true and scene_ok true. 2d skipped ranks 1 and 2 for rank 5. Cost was total: this was the only issue in condition oc1_30375086ad2fd9f6, Terra correctly answered the siding claim it was shown, and a human-graded exact/warranted condition was excluded (reason_code verdict_unsupported). Caveat 2d cannot fix by itself: exterior_door_paint_failure's atomic_claim says 'exterior door paint' while the reviewer records the door leaf as sound, so a correct selection would still have handed Terra a claim narrower than the defect - the residual is the catalog wording observation recorded in this cluster, not a further 2d fault.

rows.note: Observation 'Painted wood trim appears weathered in places.' Frozen list: exterior_door_paint_failure#1, soffit_or_porch_ceiling_weathered#2, deck_surface_weathering#3, fence_weathered#4, exterior_siding_discoloration_fading#5, shed_exterior_paint_failure#6, baseboard_wear_scuffs#7, patio_or_porch_surface_wear#8. 2d passed over its own rank-1 candidate and resolved to rank 5, the same landing as the other case. Logged even though it cost nothing: this house genuinely has painted wood siding, the condition's other two issues (33eb0f5e5ad3de52 and 81fdc4d589939872, both true siding observations) carried it, all three collapsed into condition oc1_b2e96c2b1020d48b, and the unit is adjudicated refuted with the item judged correct. It is logged because it is the second instance of the same selection behaviour and is the reason to treat the pattern as systematic rather than as one bad call - and because the collapse of three issues into one condition is exactly what hid it.

rows.case_ref: rc_eccd12ababc5 / issue 7569c5ab9b09e455 (redfin_11079485, run 20260817_224118_67317092, photo_005.jpg, 2a/2b observation 'The shower trim is old.', 2c kind modernization, scene bathroom, routing_reason exact_kind, resolution_path llm)
rows.note:
Confusion family, stated in full: cross-trade head-word homograph: 'trim' as plumbing valve trim (escutcheon, handle, tub spout, shower arm; trade plumbing / bathroom_fixtures_tile) versus 'trim' as interior millwork (baseboard, door and window casing, crown; trade trim_doors_windows). The selector took the millwork sense inside a bathroom scene whose candidate list was otherwise entirely bathroom-modernization items.
The selector passed over the rank-1 candidate, which was kind_ok true and scene_ok true, for the rank-3 candidate, on an issue where the rank-1 item's own embed_text names 'dated faucet or hardware'. Terra then correctly rejected the substituted claim and the condition was excluded (reason_code verdict_unsupported), so a real dated-fixtures observation went unbilled. Consequence is not cosmetic: outdated_bathroom_finishes is severity 3, tier work, and the package_DRIVER for bathroom_modernization, whereas dated_interior_trim is severity 1, tier optional and only package_support. Diagnostic value for a 2d prompt or selection fix: the useful signal is the mismatch between the observation's subject trade and the selected item's trade_bucket when a same-kind, same-scene candidate of the observation's own trade is ranked above it. The catalog is deliberately unchanged; do not implement this as a catalog guardrail. Frozen attribution independently agrees (stage 2d, downstream, medium confidence).
rows.checkpoint_note: dated_interior_trim is now no_action, so this row costs nothing: it is a naming and display question, not a billing one.
